dedupe_keys.name: apis peer to peer battery sharing platform

description: APIS, the Autonomous Power Interchange System, is Sony Computer Science Laboratories software for coordinating peer-to-peer electricity sharing among distributed batteries. Its README describes physical power transfers by constant-current control and a trading layer that matches surplus and deficit under energy and price conditions. Users configure participating storage devices, their metering and exchange rules; outputs are controlled transfers and transaction information in a microgrid. Geographic coverage follows an implementation, not a public fixed network. GitHub metadata states Apache-2.0 licensing. A limitation is that the repository describes an operational control system, not an independently validated simulator or a public battery telemetry archive. Safety, hardware compatibility and local electricity rules would matter in any deployment. Its reference architecture can inform microgrid and agent-based energy-sharing simulation. The related OSeMOSYS catalogue model is a long-term optimiser, not a peer-to-peer controller. No firmware, credentials or hardware configuration were downloaded.
